memories.content: HCI reviewers find it difficult to assess the reproducibility of results if the prototype version used in the evaluation is not disclosed.
Record the manipulated and fixed elements of compared design alternatives so that other researchers can reconstruct them.
Records of formative evaluation decisions enable the reconstruction of connections between raw data, interpretation, and design modifications.
The user must make it possible to trace which observations each prototype version reflects so the process of deriving design knowledge can be reviewed.
Keep the main text to the total and major categories, and place quantities, unit rates, and assumptions in one compact budget table or appendix.
Give each cost category, quantity, unit rate, and subtotal a stable row in the separate budget table.
Put the estimate basis in a dedicated table column so one assumption can be checked or revised without rewriting the narrative.
Readers can verify arithmetic and compare categories faster in a consistent table than in amounts distributed across prose.
Revise one table row and its subtotal when an estimate changes instead of repeating the new amount across several prose paragraphs.
Keep detailed arithmetic out of the main argument when readers can reach the complete table from a clear reference.
The user tends to interrupt the argument with long cost enumerations when no separate budget table is available.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate documentation concerns: the reference frame focuses on reconstructing prototype evolution and evaluation evidence, while the compared frame focuses on structuring budget details for verification, revision, and narrative clarity. Neither frame supplies a scope-aligned counterpart to the other.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame states the reproducibility consequence of omitting the evaluated prototype version.
relations.summary: Evaluation reports should disclose the prototype version used so reviewers can assess reproducibility.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame specifies recording experimental variation and controls to permit reconstruction.
relations.summary: Compared design alternatives should document which elements were manipulated and which remained fixed.

relations.reason: The reference memories jointly describe complementary parts of one traceability chain for reviewing how design knowledge was derived; the compared frame has no counterpart.
relations.summary: Formative evaluation records should trace evidence and observations through interpretation to prototype versions and design modifications.

relations.reason: The compared memories restate one presentation policy separating detailed calculations from the main argument; the reference frame does not address budget placement.
relations.summary: Detailed budget arithmetic should be kept in an accessible table or appendix while the main text presents totals and major categories.

relations.reason: The compared memories split one row-based maintenance practice into table structure and update behavior; the reference frame has no budget-maintenance counterpart.
relations.summary: Budget categories and calculations should occupy stable rows so changed estimates and subtotals can be revised locally.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame specifies a separate structural location for estimate assumptions and their isolated revision.
relations.summary: Each estimate basis should appear in a dedicated table column so assumptions can be checked or revised independently.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame states this reader-facing verification and comparison benefit.
relations.summary: A consistent budget table helps readers verify arithmetic and compare cost categories efficiently.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame identifies this recurring narrative problem caused by the absence of a separate table.
relations.summary: Without a separate budget table, long cost enumerations tend to interrupt the main argument.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame uniquely advocates a separate, consistently structured budget table that supports arithmetic checks, localized estimate revisions, and a concise main argument while addressing the disruption caused by prose-based cost enumeration.
reports.reference_only: The reference frame uniquely covers prototype-version disclosure, controlled design comparisons, and traceability from observations and raw evaluation data through interpretation to design changes.
